name: Emerald Tyre Manufacturers Limited
summary:
Hold — unresolved acquisition economics and funding. BQS 4.60 and GQS 4.40 describe an established niche tyre exporter with modest demonstrated growth, declining capital efficiency and weak cash after financing costs. IAS is NS because acquired SA Rubber earnings, debt, minority economics and current funding have not been verified. Quality rankings remain eligible at Medium confidence; investment-attractiveness ranking does not.
FY26 consolidated operating revenue rose 9.37% to ₹218.1596 crore, but core EBIT fell to ₹20.5161 crore and PAT was essentially flat at ₹10.3249 crore. Reported P/E of 12.82× masks greater reliance on forex/other income, leverage and the 34.41% IPO increase in share count. A conditional base model exceeds the 15% return hurdle only with uncommitted financing and an incomplete acquired-company perimeter. That is a sensitivity, not an ordinary investable return. Research priority is resolving acquisition terms and the post-March funding bridge, then testing new-capacity cash conversion. This is not an evidence-backed compounder or a buy recommendation. [S1,S4,S7,S8,M1]

GOV.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: Unmodified audit, explicit remuneration/RPT disclosure, and no evidenced fraud or default.
A ₹12.23 crore connected acquisition follows a ₹6.8036 crore receivable; independent valuation and cash split are missing.

GOV.contrary_evidence: The pledge was disclosed and the acquisition is a fresh issue with an arms-length statement, not proven direct promoter payment.
GOV.reason: Adequate disclosure, but material connected capital allocation remains unresolved.

MOAT.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: Industrial qualification, approximately 1,400 SKUs and distribution stock support switching friction.
July 2024 top-ten customer concentration was 65.45%, with no guaranteed long-term contracts.

MOAT.contrary_evidence: Long operating history and replacement demand support real capabilities.
MOAT.reason: Moderate niche capability, not demonstrated structural pricing power.

REV.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: FY23–26 sales of 163.9395 to 218.1596 give 9.992626884% CAGR, strictly below 10%.
Comparable H1/H2 FY26 growth of 6.78/11.90% does not justify an adjustment; five-year CAGR is ND.

REV.contrary_evidence: Four-year growth of 13.03% and capacity expansion are favorable context, not substitutes chosen for scoring.
REV.reason: Starting score 4, adjustment zero, Medium-confidence ceiling 8. No rounding into score 6.

DUR.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

New lines remained in trial in September, with customer/country concentration and funding limits.

DUR.contrary_evidence: Mixing and solar were commissioned and existing utilization is about 90%.
DUR.reason: Plausible runway, but not contracted or proven cash-generative growth.

CAP.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: Restricted-cash-retained ROIC declined from 14.06% to 9.90% to 7.29% in FY24–26.
FY23–26 incremental NOPAT/IC is 2.31%; IC reconciles to 239.2716 on both sides.

CAP.contrary_evidence: New capacity has not yet had a full earnings period, so this is not a final project IRR.
CAP.reason: Recent reinvestment has not demonstrated returns above a 12–15% capital-cost test.

CASH.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: FY24–26 CFO/PAT is 1.2685 before finance but .2456 after finance.
Three-year cash after interest/capex is −88.3294; capital-advance reclassification preserves FCF.

CASH.contrary_evidence: Reported CFO is positive in all five observations and expansion capex is real.
CASH.reason: Modest conversion after financing, not persistent negative operating CFO; no automatic low-factor cap.

BAL.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: Net debt/core EBITDA is 4.51× and core EBIT/interest 1.50×.
WC utilization is 94%, current maturity 15.4186, and acquired claims are unknown.

BAL.contrary_evidence: CARE upgraded to BBB/A3+ and assessed liquidity adequate with 11.79 liquid funds.
BAL.reason: Leveraged and sensitive to refinancing, but no evidenced current default.

New lines were still in trial after earlier completion expectations.

EXEC.contrary_evidence: Mixing and 1 MW solar were achieved; power/rain delays were explained.
EXEC.reason: Concrete achievements coexist with guidance and timing misses.

EARN.recovery_score_source: Exact Scorecard and Calculation Audit narrative; NS is retained as null.

material_facts.text: Core EBIT declined from 24.1352 in FY24 to 20.5161 in FY26; PAT was flat year-on-year.
Forex gains of 6.4820 dominate other income; no-other-income normalized PAT is 5.10645.

EARN.contrary_evidence: Forex gains may economically offset export realizations; not all other income is nonrecurring.
EARN.reason: Core and per-share earning progress is weaker than revenue growth.

Target earnings, external claims, minority rights and actual pre-entry funding are unverified.

sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved acquisition economics and funding. BQS 4.60 and GQS 4.40 describe an established niche tyre exporter with modest demonstrated growth, declining capital efficiency and weak cash after financing costs. IAS is NS because acquired SA Rubber earnings, debt, minority economics and current funding have not been verified. Quality rankings remain eligible at Medium confidence; investment-attractiveness ranking does not.
FY26 consolidated operating revenue rose 9.37% to ₹218.1596 crore, but core EBIT fell to ₹20.5161 crore and PAT was essentially flat at ₹10.3249 crore. Reported P/E of 12.82× masks greater reliance on forex/other income, leverage and the 34.41% IPO increase in share count. A conditional base model exceeds the 15% return hurdle only with uncommitted financing and an incomplete acquired-company perimeter. That is a sensitivity, not an ordinary investable return. sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Deep research under v3.0; evidence cutoff 20 October 2026 and official NSE closing quote ₹67.95 on 19 October. Documents were retrieved on 21 October but only pre-cutoff information is used. Identity is verified: Emerald Tyre Manufacturers Limited, ETML, INE0RHD01013, NSE SME SM series, 1,200-share lot, 19,476,512 shares and market capitalization ₹132.3429 crore. Listing date was 12 December 2024. Issuer letters sometimes label the series EQ; the dated exchange master and actual prints establish SM. A closing price is not an executable offer. No user position is supplied, so ₹5 lakh is solely the framework's illustrative liquidity reference.
Historical scope is the consolidated parent and wholly owned Belgian/UAE subsidiaries through March 2026. SA Rubber became a 64.44%-owned subsidiary on 25 September 2026; its missing accounts cannot be treated as if they were part of March history. Five audited annual observations, FY22–26, are available. FY22/23 use the IPO restatement; FY24–26 use the latest annual-report comparatives. Earnings and cash-policy differences are explicitly bridged. Five observations are not enough for a five-year CAGR. The latest audited comparable period is FY26, with H1/H2 detail; CARE's unaudited five-month FY27 total operating income of ₹102 crore is not an audited TTM or annualized earnings forecast.
G1 Integrity is Conditional: disclosed related-party acquisition, but independent valuation and transaction composition are unverified; no evidenced severe abuse. G2 Reliability is Conditional: core audited totals remain usable after restatement, cash-presentation and EPS-denominator reconciliation. G3 Funding is Hold — unresolved: actual current funding and acquired claims are missing; modeled deficits are not proof of default. G4 Tradability is Conditional: active SM but limited whole-lot capacity and official irregular-trading/fewer-than-100-PAN alerts. Historical quality confidence is Medium, full-group valuation Low, market retrieval High and practical implementation Medium. [S1–S4,S7,S8,M1–M5]

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
The canonical factors are GOV 5, MOAT 5, REV 4, DUR 6, CAP 4, CASH 4, BAL 4, EXEC 4 and EARN 4, all at Medium confidence. R and P are NS at Low confidence. D is 1 at Medium confidence because credible stress severely impairs equity; this does not assert current insolvency. L is 1 at Medium confidence after lot-discrete execution tests.
Exact Decimal calculations: BQS = .20×5 + .20×5 + .12×4 + .10×6 + .12×4 + .10×4 + .08×4 + .08×4 = 4.60. GQS = .40×4 + .20×6 + .15×4 + .15×4 + .10×4 = 4.40. No numerical cap changes either result. GOV exceeds 3 and G1 has not failed; CASH and CAP at 4 do not trigger the low-factor growth-quality cap. Scores are reused unchanged between formulas.
IAS has known contribution .25×4.60 + .20×1 + .10×1 = 1.45 and weighted coverage 55%. R's 35% and P's 10% remain missing, with no redistribution or neutral score. Its mathematical 1–10 bound is 1.90–5.95, not a statistical interval or rankable point estimate. All material quality factors are Medium and G2 has not failed, so BQS/GQS remain ranking-eligible despite G3 Hold and IAS NS. Rankings remain provisional until the full universe is complete. Each factor's material and contrary evidence is in Appendix B. [E1–E13]

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text:
Emerald manufactures industrial/off-highway tyres, especially solid resilient, pneumatic and press-on-band tyres, with rims and fitment solutions. Industrial buyers value load capacity, application suitability, durability and reduced equipment downtime. Manufacturing is at Gummidipoondi near Chennai; Belgian/UAE distribution and stock support export replacement customers. Disclosed brands include GRECKSTER, EMPOWER and AXIMO.
FY26 consolidated exports were ₹174.6012 crore, approximately 80% of operating revenue. The parent's 74.42% export mix is a different scope, not a contradiction. Domestic sales were ₹41.4939 crore, with operating incentives completing the revenue bridge. CARE reports replacement demand above 90%, OEM about 9%, solid tyres about 51%, pneumatic about 41%, approximately 1,400 SKUs, 30 international dealers and 45 domestic franchisees. The broad catalog supports availability but consumes inventory and tooling capital.
FY26 sales exposure included the US ₹67 crore, Russia ₹33 crore and Europe ₹39 crore. Country, customer, currency and distributor risks therefore matter. Replacement demand is not contracted subscription revenue; the prospectus warns that key customers need not have long-term contracts. Consolidated accounts eliminate intercompany sales, so subsidiary gross turnover must not be added again. Capacity, dealer counts and global TAM are operating context, not recognized revenue. Rubber, chemicals, steel and energy affect unit economics. [S1,S3,S4,S6]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
A plausible narrow moat combines industrial application qualification, compounds and molds, a large replacement catalog, nearby distribution inventory and service familiarity. An established tyre that reduces downtime can be sticky. Two decades of operations and repeated exports support capability. They do not demonstrate durable pricing power: verified market share, persistent price premium and customer-retention cohorts were not located. Core EBITDA margin of 12.60% and declining ROIC argue against assuming a strong moat from niche status alone.
For the four months to July 2024, top 1/3/5/10 customers contributed 26.47/49.01/55.32/65.45% of revenue; top 1/3/5/10 suppliers represented 23.09/54.25/68.63/81.51%. These are dated concentration observations, not current percentages. Customer destocking, raw-material pressure and financing constraints can coincide. Replacement demand spans installed equipment but still varies with utilization and industrial activity. BKT and TVS have far greater resources and distribution, while local/Asian manufacturers constrain pricing. MOAT 5 recognizes qualification friction and a useful catalog without asserting proven structural excess returns. [S3,S4,P1,P2]

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Consolidated operating revenue for FY22–26 was ₹133.6426/163.9395/170.9874/199.4680/218.1596 crore. Annual additions in FY23–26 were ₹30.2969/7.0479/28.4806/18.6916 crore, with growth of 22.67/4.30/16.66/9.37%. The preselected FY23–26 three-year CAGR is 9.992626884%, strictly below 10%, so REV starts at 4. Rounding it to 10.0% cannot move it into the score-6 band. A verified FY21 group endpoint is unavailable, so five-year CAGR is ND; ten-year CAGR is also ND. Four-year FY22–26 CAGR of 13.03% is context, not a more favorable replacement for the required scoring window. Revenue endpoints are unchanged across the identified FY24 original/restated reconciliation.
H1 FY26 revenue ₹105.2165 crore versus ₹98.5346 crore grew 6.78%; H2 ₹112.9431 versus ₹100.9334 crore grew 11.90%. This does not establish a sustained step-change warranting an adjustment, so REV remains 4. Foreign subsidiaries' FY26 turnover of ₹53.5205 crore is before eliminations and must not inflate group sales. CARE's five-month FY27 ₹102 crore total operating income has no verified comparable five-month base or profit; no annualization is presented as fact.
Existing utilization/distribution support volume, while mix and currency affect realizations. New lines were still in trial in September 2026. SA Rubber is a post-FY26 acquisition and did not drive historical group growth. Exact volume, price/mix and currency contributions are undisclosed; organic constant-currency growth is ND. No acquisition haircut is invented. CARE's 10,800 MT existing capacity at 90% implies around 9,720 MT, while 16,240 MT at 85–90% utilization implies about 13,800–14,600 MT. Product mix and group transfers prevent treating a revenue-per-ton proxy as verified unit economics. [S1–S4,S6]

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Capacity disclosures differ by date and product scope. FY24 prospectus capacity/utilization: solid 5,920 MT/70.89%, press-on 900/67.88%, pneumatic 3,360/90.50% and rims 380/62.32%. July 2026 presentation uses 10,560 MT; September CARE uses 10,800 existing at 90% and 16,240 expanded, with new lines expected commercially in H2 FY27 after trials. These overlapping descriptions are not additive. Commissioned mixing and a 1 MW solar facility supplying about 30% of power are useful achieved milestones, unlike merely announced capacity.
Invested capital is equity plus gross debt minus unrestricted cash and liquid mutual funds; restricted deposits remain capital. FY22–26 IC is ₹102.5947/119.6822/137.7157/182.9933/239.2716 crore. Core EBIT excludes other income. At 25% normalized tax, NOPAT on average IC gives FY23–26 ROIC of 11.36/14.06/9.90/7.29%. This is an explicit analyst measure, not the issuer's ROCE. Operating lease rent remains an expense and is not also capitalized without verified lease obligations. FY23–26 incremental NOPAT ₹2.76555 crore divided by incremental IC ₹119.5894 crore yields 2.31%. New capacity has an earnings lag, so that is realized group efficiency, not final project IRR. Current returns fall below an analyst nominal-INR cost-of-capital test of 12–15%; the separate equity-return hurdle is 15%.
The FY26 asset-side IC bridge also equals ₹239.2716 crore: PPE 130.1601 + ONWC including SA 109.0844 + security deposits 2.5489 + staff loans 1.2140 + restricted FD 4.6296 − non-WC current claims 3.6284 − deferred-tax/noncurrent-employee claims 4.7370. IC increased 56.2783: PPE +44.0222, capital advances −9.9445 and remaining net operating capital +22.2006. Reclassified cash capex 41.0594 less DA 6.9723 and disposal/rounding .0094 equals 34.0777, matching PPE plus capital-advance change. The residual includes working capital, tax, provisions, deposits and FX; it is not an invented acquisition return.
Base growth of 10/12/10/8/6%, core margins rising to 15%, WC intensity declining to 45% and cash capex ₹4/5/6/7/7 crore are analyst assumptions. They presume a productive ramp of already-built assets and maintenance/debottlenecking, not contracted demand. Bull requires more favorable mix and productivity. CAP 4 and GQS 4.40 distinguish accessible capacity from demonstrated value-creating reinvestment. [S1–S6,S9]

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Chairman/MD V T Chandhrasekharan and whole-time director D Eswara Krishnan have longstanding tyre experience. Their combined remuneration in FY22–26 was ₹.9796/1.2010/1.3111/1.1377/1.1377 crore. FY26 CMD ₹.7134 and WTD ₹.4243 were unchanged. Broad KMP/related expenses of ₹3.2431 crore include CEO/CFO/CS, not just promoters; father's consultancy ₹.7260 and related rent ₹.2064 warrant scrutiny. Broad expense was about 31.4% of group PAT; the two executive directors about 11.0%. Proposed annual CMD/WTD rates of ₹.9624/.5256 effective 25 November 2026 are announced future terms, not FY26 costs.
March promoters held 9,798,828 shares, 50.31%. Pledged 939,500 shares represented 9.59% of promoter holding and about 4.82% of all shares. The pledge is disclosed in both prospectus and annual report. A secondary September figure of 50.45% was not treated as verified current ownership. IPO fresh issuance of 4,986,000 shares at ₹95 increased shares 34.41%, from 14,490,512 to 19,476,512, raising gross ₹47.367 crore. June 2025 utilization: capex 26.3816, general corporate purposes 8.5071, expenses 2.525 and earmarked remaining capex 9.9532. CARE September says proceeds were deployed for capex. The earlier unspent balance is not an additional current cash pot. No new FY26 issuance/options/warrants were verified in reviewed records.
SA Rubber is controlled by the MD's brother. Outstanding receivables in FY22–26 were ₹3.5200/5.7168/5.2774/6.4657/6.8036 crore, versus FY26 sales to it of ₹1.4618 crore. January's proposal allowed up to ₹14 crore of cash/noncash fresh subscription, called terms arms-length, and disclosed target turnover falling from ZAR 9.13 million to 8.30 million to 7.45 million in FY23–25. September completion was ₹12.23 crore for 4,100 shares and 64.44%. Fresh issuance is not proof of direct payment to the promoter, but independent valuation, target profit/debt/cash and exact noncash conversion were not located. Minority ownership of 35.56% prevents allocating all target earnings to listed shareholders.
December guidance of FY26 group sales ₹250 crore, parent ₹228 crore and debt ₹110 crore was missed: group sales were 218.16 and debt 135.69; new lines remained in trial in September. Management cited power/rain delays; achieved mixing/solar and the CARE upgrade are contrary evidence to blanket execution failure. Audit is unmodified; CARO reports no default/fraud and regular undisputed statutory dues. Bank stock returns were lower than books, with the company stating no drawing-power/security impact. Vehicle-charge compounding is pending. Tax appeals and documentation issues are not convictions. CARO lists disputed tax amounts totaling ₹4.2673 crore at CIT(A)/ITAT, while note 29 shows ₹5.5863 crore including demand/interest detail. The difference was not fully reconciled; the larger note-29 amount is used once in stress, not added to the CARO amount. GOV 5 and EXEC 4 reflect the mixed record. [S1–S5,S7–S10]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Core EBITDA in FY22–26 was ₹15.6597/21.0319/29.6644/27.0599/27.4884 crore; core EBIT was 12.2118/16.8287/24.1352/21.1735/20.5161. Core EBITDA margin peaked at 17.35% in FY24, then 13.57% and 12.60%. Other income rose from ₹.9810 to 3.1467 to 6.9851 crore in FY24–26; FY26 forex gains of 6.4820 dominate. Management's ₹34.4735 crore EBITDA includes other income. Forex can economically offset export realizations and is not automatically nonrecurring or improper. Nevertheless a conservative no-other-income, 25%-tax normalized PAT is ₹5.10645 crore versus reported 10.3249. Both definitions are shown.
H2 FY26 core EBITDA ₹12.5197 crore/11.08% margin and PAT 2.7661 were weaker than H1 core EBITDA 14.9687 and prior H2 PAT 4.0511. FY26 diluted EPS was ₹5.30 versus FY25 ₹6.52 using the later report's weighted shares. The earlier FY25 report's ₹5.36 uses ending shares. PAT does not differ; the denominator does. Current-share EPS 5.36 to 5.30 shows essentially flat per-share profit rather than a fabricated operating collapse from changed share counts.
FY24–26 CFO of ₹12.4285/8.1557/20.5712 crore totals 41.1554 against PAT 32.4450, or 1.2685× before financing interest. Subtract finance cash of 33.1865 and conversion is only .2456×. Cash capex totals 96.2983; CFO less capex is −55.1429 and after finance −88.3294. All five annual observations have negative post-interest/capex cash flow. Expansion explains investment but does not fund it.
FY26 CFO includes release/reclassification of ₹9.9445 crore prior capital advances. Moving it jointly between operating and investing gives analytical FY26 CFO 10.6267/capex 41.0594 and FY25 CFO 18.1002/capex 41.1364. Each year's FCF and combined cash stay unchanged. The cash-flow liability subtotal uses a cash-use convention: 28.2883 operating profit +2.3327 asset adjustments −5.1529 liability subtotal =25.4681 pretax cash, less 4.8969 tax =20.5712 CFO. Trade payables fell 6.4775; their positive line belongs to a subtotal that is subtracted. It is not fictitious cash inflow. FY25 similarly reconciles 27.6366−23.3817−(−7.6847)=11.9396. Cash roll 15.597+20.5712−57.9391+32.3167≈10.5458 versus 10.5456 reported differs only by rounding. MF purchases and consolidation/translation adjustments are not operating cash.
IPO restatement changes original FY22/23/24 PAT 4.6366/7.3435/11.6867 to 4.8462/8.9285/12.1432. Drivers include employee obligations, forex/export-benefit cutoff, unrealized inventory profit, depreciation/useful lives and tax. FY24 prospectus CFO 17.1208 differs from later annual 12.4285; DA 5.0157 differs from 5.5292. The latest FY24–26 annual baseline and earlier restated years remain separately labeled, rather than claiming a seamless five-year cash conversion series. Average receivable days rose 68.67/77.98/78.25/82.64 in FY23–26. Inventory days 194.96/221.37/198.37/210.15 use materials plus stock changes, not full COGS. Receivables older than six months of ₹2.195 crore are considered good; no material bad-debt provision was located. Related balances and currency exposure require collection evidence. [S1–S3,S5,S6]

sections.title: 10. Balance Sheet, Funding & Survival
sections.text:
March gross debt ₹135.6909 crore comprises long-term 57.6561 and short-term 78.0348. Short-term debt already includes current term maturities 15.4186; these are not added twice. Cash/bank 10.5456 includes deposits 4.6296. Note 50 loosely describes the full balance as available excluding lien, although note 19 includes deposits. Prudently available current cash 5.916 plus mutual funds 5.8769 equals 11.7929, matching CARE's ₹11.79 crore liquidity. Deposits are not credited as free acquisition/capex funding. Net debt is 123.898, 4.51× core EBITDA; core EBIT/interest is 1.50×. CARE's 2.50× coverage uses a different, other-income-inclusive definition.
CARE upgraded to BBB/A3+ in September and called liquidity adequate, with gross cash accrual 18.77 versus FY27 repayments 15.42. WC utilization of 94% through June and the annual report's statement of no undrawn facilities constrain assumed headroom. Rated facilities of ₹125 crore are not undrawn available cash.
Every opening balance has one model disposition. ONWC 102.2808 excludes the SA receivable 6.8036. Statutory dues, capital creditors, other current liabilities and net current tax total 3.6284, paid once by FY27 end. Deferred tax 4.3841 and noncurrent employee provision .3529 remain a terminal claim of 4.7370. Current employees/warranty provisions, dealers and payables are already in ONWC. Security deposits/staff loans have no free-cash recovery. The recommended FY26 dividend of ₹1 per share, totaling ₹1.9476512 crore, is conservatively modeled as a pre-entry cash use. The notice sets 17 September as the record date and payment within the stipulated period if AGM-approved; actual approval/payment was not separately verified. No income is credited to an October buyer.
Acquisition cash of 5.4264–12.23 is an analyst bound assuming zero to 6.8036 of the existing SA receivable might be converted, not disclosed transaction terms. The source receivable is neither collected through ONWC nor added again as terminal recovery. Remaining target value is not a free asset; target external claims and minority rights remain missing for full-group valuation.
No-new-financing bear/base/bull cases have modeled deficits, but the reconstruction includes an unobserved April–October bridge and an acquisition that actually completed. This identifies missing funding information, not an actual default. Essential no-growth retains the completed acquisition, maturity, announced dividend, opening claims, ₹3 crore maintenance and 12.6% margin, with a 5.1889 deficit. A favorable essential bound at 15% margin, ₹2 crore maintenance, 9.5% interest and lower acquisition cash stays funded with minimum cash .2468. That counterexample, the rating upgrade and completed investment support G3 Hold rather than forced Fail. Unknown later maturities remain debt at exit; separate ₹10 crore/year amortization is a sensitivity, not a fabricated obligation. [S1,S4,S7,S8]

sections.title: 11. Valuation, Five-Year Funding & Reverse Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹67.95, market cap is ₹132.3429 crore and EV ₹256.2409 after only available cash/MF. Reported P/E is 12.82×; no-other-income normalized P/E 25.92×; core EV/EBITDA 9.32×; P/B 1.15×. There is no peer-P/E average assembled from unmatched quote dates. A capital-intensive EV/EBITDA framework is useful only when depreciation, maintenance/growth investment, working capital and all equity claims are modeled.
The preferred dated_model.py begins with audited March 2026 balances, reconstructs an explicitly estimated pre-entry bridge to 19 October, then models remaining FY27, FY28–31 and a terminal stub to 19 October 2031. Entry-to-exit is exactly five years. March balances are not claimed as observed October balances. Operating annual run rates are prorated for stubs; the terminal annual run rate extends the final growth assumption. The completed acquisition and announced dividend are pre-entry uses; current maturity and other opening claims are paid by March 2027. The earlier fiscal-only checkpoint is superseded for return calculations.
Bear assumptions: sales growth −10/0/3/5/5%, core margins 9→11%, WC 54→50% of sales, capex ₹3/3/4/4/4 crore, 11% interest and 6× terminal EBITDA. Base: growth 10/12/10/8/6%, margins 13.5→15%, WC 47→45%, capex 4/5/6/7/7, 10% interest and 8× exit. Bull: growth 18/18/15/12/10%, margins 15→17%, WC 45→42%, capex 5/7/9/10/11, 9.5% interest and 10× exit. DA ranges ₹8–11 crore and normalized tax is 25% on positive pretax profit, with no invented tax refund. These are analyst scenarios, not management commitments. No rescue funds are assumed received in ordinary cases. Negative cash remains an explicit deficit and ordinary IRR is NS. Separately labeled rescue cases solve interest, tax and new debt jointly and deduct the resulting debt at exit.
Date-matched conditional rescue prices are ₹3.94/170.62/374.29 for bear/base/bull, with conditional IRRs −43.43%/20.22%/40.67%. Uncommitted new debt required is ₹26.3394/20.2144/19.0356 crore. Lower-bound base acquisition cash reduces required debt to 13.2368 and gives a conditional 20.89%, still not an ordinary funded case. The favorable essential legacy case is funded and returns 5.99%, below the hurdle, but cannot represent unknown SA economics. Later amortization and equity rescue at 0/20/40% issue-price discounts are separately modeled.
At a 15% hurdle and 15% core margin, conditional required constant growth is 11.15% at a 6× exit, 5.27% at 8× and 1.11% at 10×, requiring new debt 18.34/13.66/10.36 respectively. The quote can therefore look undemanding only with financing, margin and terminal assumptions. It does not prove a cheap funded business. A full 12/15/17% margin by 6/8/10× multiple grid and 12/15/18% hurdle entry sensitivities accompany the model. These are conditional diagnostics, not targets or buy levels. Missing target accounts and current funding keep R/P NS. [S1,S4,S7,S8,M1; model appendices]

sections.title: 12. Liquidity & Implementation
sections.text:
All 60 official full-market NSE archives from 24 July to 19 October were available and hashed. Five ETML-absent/no-recorded-print sessions, 31 July, 20 August, 21/23/25 September, are retained as zero-trade observations, not missing files. Actual traded value is used, not OHLC multiplied by volume. The 60-day mean is ₹11.73569 lakh and median ₹6.92910 lakh; the conservative denominator is the lower median. The 20-day mean/median are ₹10.88883/6.92880 lakh, with three zero days versus five over 60. On 19 October, 6,000 shares, ₹4.077 lakh and five trades printed; none establishes live depth.
Continuous liquidation of the ₹5 lakh reference takes 14.43 sessions at 5% participation, 36.08 at 2%, and 7.22 at 10%. This gives starting L 3, downgraded to L 1 after whole-lot tests and restrictions. At ₹81,540 per 1,200-share lot, six lots equal ₹489,240 and seven ₹570,780. At 5%, only 10/60 days admit one full lot; aggregate capacity is 18 lots, implying 20/23.33 sessions for six/seven lots at the observed mean rate. Median daily whole-lot capacity is zero. At 2%, only two eligible days and three total lots imply 120/140 sessions; at 10%, 23 eligible days and 52 lots imply 6.92/8.08. These are historical capacities, not promised fills. Seven-lot start windows completed 48/60, with completed-only median 19.5 and maximum 37 sessions; twelve censored paths prevent interpreting that median as an unbiased wait forecast.
REG1's irregular-SME and fewer-than-100-unique-PAN indicators are 0, meaning the category applies. Named GSM, long/short ASM, ESM and default indicators are 100, meaning not under those named measures, not risk-free. The 19 October file is designated effective 21 October and is distinguished from actual quote-date trading. Active SM and a 20% price band, ₹54.40–81.50, do not remove one-sided circuit risk. March promoter holding implies nominal public holding 49.69%, not verified liquid free float. Current ownership, live spread and depth remain unverified. G4 is Conditional; implementation requires current order-book, lot, band and position checks. [M1–M5,S1,S10]

sections.title: 13. Peer Checks & Multibagger Feasibility
sections.text:
Primary peer comparisons retain scope and definitions. BKT FY26 consolidated revenue ₹10,823.08 crore, core EBITDA 2,300.43/21.25% margin, PAT 1,243.10, CFO 2,249.32 and capex 3,003.29 show much greater specialty-OHT scale and margins. Yet cash after interest/capex is −863.13, demonstrating that even a leader funds expansion. Scale, integration and geography make its valuation multiple nontransferable.
TVS Srichakra FY26 consolidated sales were ₹3,643.35 crore, core EBITDA 278.99/7.66%, PAT 71.06, owner PAT 71.23, CFO 296.99 and capex 110.50. Core EBITDA excludes other income and exceptional items; a ₹22.43 crore grant accounting adjustment still needs normalization before calling the margin recurring. Its two/three-wheeler and OHT mix differs from Emerald.
Tolins standalone CARE figures show FY26 total operating income ₹223.25 versus 178.75, PBILDT 24.89 versus 30.94 and PAT 15.04 versus 20.76: sales growth need not mean stronger economics. TOI/PBILDT are not silently renamed comparable core sales/EBITDA. Missing CFO/ROIC remain ND. CARE's July withdrawal followed surrendered bank facilities/no outstanding balance and unavailed proposed facilities; earlier June issuer noncooperation is context, not current payment default. No peer valuation ranking is asserted without matching prices and claim adjustments.
A 5×/10× thesis was not requested and is unsupported. Five-year 10× appreciation requires 58.49% annually, far above demonstrated sales growth. The conditional bull price is about 5.51× entry only under optimistic operating/multiple assumptions, uncommitted funding and missing acquired claims. That is not a supported 5× outcome. Capacity alone does not establish per-share wealth creation after financing and dilution. [P1–P3,S1,S4]

sections.title: 14. Bear Case, Falsification & Monitoring
sections.text:
The key falsification variable is cash conversion of expanded capacity, not installed tonnage. A credible linked path is dealer/customer weakness, lower utilization, weaker mix and raw-material pass-through, slower collections/inventory buildup, tighter bank lines, expensive refinancing or dilution, then little residual equity. Stress combines sales growth −20/−5/3/5/5%, margins 7→10%, WC 60→53%, 12% interest, capex ₹3/3/3/4/4, a 5× exit and ₹7.6445 crore disclosed tax/DGFT claims paid once. Conditional new debt required is 72.7454 and terminal equity is zero. Ordinary bear, even after conditional funding of 26.3394, loses 94.21% per share. This is permanent-loss analysis, not a claim about near-term quoted volatility.
The strongest contrary facts are a working plant, replacement demand, commissioned mixing/solar, CARE's upgrade, actual acquisition completion and a favorable essential case that can fund known claims. They stop an unsupported G3 Fail or fraud conclusion. Conversely, a few strong sales periods or a low P/E do not resolve missing target debt and minority claims. Improved classification needs complete SA accounts/terms, actual funding, ramp profitability and cash receipts. Tax claims remain appeals/disputes, not convictions; any allegation of abuse requires corroboration.
Eight company-specific monitoring items in Appendix G cover commissioning, core margin, cash after finance, WC/collections, bank headroom/maturities, SA transaction economics, governance/contingencies and whole-lot liquidity. Baselines, expected milestones, warning levels and thesis-break events are distinguished. The suggested review cadence is attached to relevant filings, not an activated reminder or automatic trade rule. [S1,S3–S8,M1–M5]

sections.title: 15. Final Classification, Action Logic & Uncertainties
sections.text:
Final classification is Hold — unresolved: a mixed-quality, capital-intensive expansion/special situation, not an evidence-backed compounder. BQS 4.60 and GQS 4.40 are complete Medium-confidence quality scores and remain ranking-eligible. IAS is NS and excluded from investment-attractiveness ranking. Investment consideration waits for acquired economics and actual financing, not merely a lower quote. No allocation or buy/sell instruction is given; the ₹5 lakh reference is not a recommended position. Existing-holder decisions would need holdings, tax and execution context that has not been supplied.
Material gaps are the actual acquisition cash/noncash split, target audited accounts and external guarantees, minority rights, post-March group cash/debt and committed undrawn facilities, future term maturities, current ownership/pledge updates, volume/price/currency decomposition, commercial ramp/utilization, sustainable maintenance investment and live bid/ask depth. A company-site/NSE announcement search was not established as exhaustive; “not located” does not mean “does not exist.” Scanned older standalone reports were preserved, while verified FY22/23 group inputs come from the prospectus restatement rather than unread scans.
Neither a positive rescue IRR nor the low funded legacy-only return can replace a supported full-group R. At the same time, G3 uncertainty does not erase usable historical quality evidence, and low quality does not itself prove overvaluation. Revisit after complete interim accounts and SA disclosures. The research is complete at the documented evidence level; the unresolved gate is the finding, not permission to invent missing facts. Universe rankings remain provisional. [S1–S10,M1–M5]

The canonical factors are GOV 5, MOAT 5, REV 4, DUR 6, CAP 4, CASH 4, BAL 4, EXEC 4 and EARN 4, all at Medium confidence. R and P are NS at Low confidence. D is 1 at Medium confidence because credible stress severely impairs equity; this does not assert current insolvency. L is 1 at Medium confidence after lot-discrete execution tests.
Exact Decimal calculations: BQS = .20×5 + .20×5 + .12×4 + .10×6 + .12×4 + .10×4 + .08×4 + .08×4 = 4.60. GQS = .40×4 + .20×6 + .15×4 + .15×4 + .10×4 = 4.40. No numerical cap changes either result. GOV exceeds 3 and G1 has not failed; CASH and CAP at 4 do not trigger the low-factor growth-quality cap. Scores are reused unchanged between formulas.
IAS has known contribution .25×4.60 + .20×1 + .10×1 = 1.45 and weighted coverage 55%. R's 35% and P's 10% remain missing, with no redistribution or neutral score. Its mathematical 1–10 bound is 1.90–5.95, not a statistical interval or rankable point estimate. All material quality factors are Medium and G2 has not failed, so BQS/GQS remain ranking-eligible despite G3 Hold and IAS NS. Rankings remain provisional until the full universe is complete.
